newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S LAND BANK IN FOR REVAMP - HANEKOM.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S LAND BANK IN FOR REVAMP - HANEKOM.

text.p: Small black farmers might in future be able to access finance from South Africa's Land Bank through post offices as part of plans to revamp the institution, Land and Agriculture Minister Derek Hanekom said on Tuesday.
Hanekom told a parliamentary agriculture committee that failure to obtain credit was one of the biggest problems facing small black farmers.

"We need an effective credit environment... It's clear that in the course of this year the Agricultural Credit Board will come to an end and the process of expanding the activities of the Land Bank will begin," he said.
Hanekom said the cabinet would soon appoint a new transitional board to start work on April 1.
"Part of our challenge is to transform the Land Bank into a professional body providing a good service, that is financially strong," he said.
"There has to be a high recovery rate when it gives loans and it has to act accordingly when people don't return their loans."
Hanekom said the bank would open some new branches but would act mainly as a wholesale finance provider, lending through other institutions.
"We're really considering using the post offices much more extensively... We intend using other institutions like co-ops, NGOs, that are already on the ground," he said.
